analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture represents WarnerMedia HBO's cloud linear playout infrastructure deployed in AWS US East 1. Master media files stored in S3 are transferred to an EC2 playout fleet running Evertz ORT software across three Availability Zones (10 channels per AZ, 30 channels total). Per Rule 4 (Dynamic Logical Fusion), the three visual EC2 instances represent identical parallel playout workloads and are fused into a single EC2 node. CloudFormation and Auto Scaling are omitted per the deployment layer omission rules as they are not active runtime flow participants. The playout unicast signal travels from EC2 across AWS Direct Connect using Evertz CloudBridge to two destinations: directly to the NYC Hudson Yards BCP satellite uplink, and to the on-premises Techwood / CNN Center facility (the tertiary X chain), which compresses the signal and sends it to the Atlanta satellite uplink for distribution.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Tandem's transaction enrichment data pipeline. It starts with an account update event on an ingestion Kinesis stream, triggering a lightweight batching Lambda function. This function reads raw transaction data for the given account from an RDS database and splits descriptions into batches of ~100 onto an SQS queue. SQS buffers and fans out processing across scalable natural language processing (NLP) Lambda workers running an ANTLR-generated parser. The NLP Lambdas persist enriched transaction data along with the model version into an RDS database and publish completion events to a downstream Kinesis stream to notify other platform services.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture represents SonarCloud by SonarSource, which performs automated code quality analysis. First, developers push code to GitHub, triggering an event captured by an AWS Lambda function that triages the event and puts an analysis request into an Amazon SQS queue. An autoscaling ECS Fargate cluster (Scanner) polls the SQS queue, clones the repository directly from GitHub into ephemeral storage, performs code analysis, and posts the resulting analysis report to an EC2 instance hosting an API/UI. The EC2 instance stores the raw report in an Amazon Aurora database. A second ECS Fargate cluster (Compute Engine) polls Aurora to extract raw reports, computes code quality metrics, updates Aurora with final results, and indexes shared optimization data in Elasticsearch (OpenSearch). Developers access the final reports through the EC2 UI and API.
